description: An explanation in steps. Screen coordinates run 0 to 1000 across the screenshot, x to the right, y down.

escalate.description: Set when the question is beyond what you can answer well here, so a slower, deeper helper can be offered: a short reason, up to 160 characters. steps may then be empty. Otherwise null.

A piece with no at appears with the words, one after another.

Lumps that overlap melt into one skin with smooth necks; soft (0.05 to 1, default 0.5) is how far they blend. Build one form per blob and join forms with tube.

addConnector.description: A rope, belt, wire, chain or pipe between two objects, following them as they move. kind straight (default) is taut and shortens as a weight rises; slack hangs in a sag; wrapped is a flat belt round two wheels. fromSide and toSide say where an end meets its object, as seen from the front (left, right, top, bottom, front, back; the rim of a wheel), else its middle; fromAnchor and toAnchor name a point of a ready-made part. radius is its thickness.

addPart.description: A ready-made part fitted to the box size [x,y,z]. Electronics: chip (variant black or metal), header (n pins per row, two rows), port (variant usb, usb3, ethernet, hdmi, usbc; its opening faces +z), lens, screen, button, fan (n blades, axis y), wheel (n spokes, axis z). Mechanism, axis y: cylinder-block (variant cutaway or finned; the bore is round in x,z), piston, connecting-rod (small end up), valve (head down), spark-plug (tip down), spring (n coils), pipe, elbow, housing (variant cutaway); axis z: crankshaft (n throws), camshaft (n lobes), gear (n teeth), bearing (n balls). Each has good proportions and named anchors for pins.

addArray.description: Copies of an existing object, count in all (the original is the first). step moves each copy [x,y,z] from the last; turn rotates each copy about the origin of the group the original sits in, which is how to put blades round a hub.

reveal.description: Draw a tube, line or arrow on, from its start: to 1 is all of it.

highlight.description: Pulse an object or mark to draw the eye, optionally in a colour.

by.description: the part that drives this one

ratio.description: with by: turns per turn of that part (default 1); -20 to 20

phase.description: with by: degrees ahead of that part; -3600 to 3600

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

spin.description: Make a part turn round its own axis and keep turning, until another spin on it says otherwise. rpm is turns a minute (negative the other way; 0 stops; dur is the time to get up to speed). Or give by, another part that drives it: it then turns ratio times as far as that part (0.5 half as fast, -1 a meshed gear) and phase degrees ahead. axis is x, y or z, default z (the axis of a crankshaft, camshaft, gear and bearing; use y for a fan).

piston.description: the id of the piston part already added (not the cylinder block, not a group)

id.description: the same as piston; piston is clearer

shaft.description: the id of the crankshaft part already added

rod.description: the id of the connecting-rod part already added, joining them

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

crank.description: Tie a piston to a spinning crankshaft through a connecting rod: the piston slides up and down its cylinder (along y, in the x,y plane) as the crank pin goes round, and the rod swings to join them. This acts on parts you have already added, by their ids; it adds nothing and a new name does nothing. Name the piston with piston (the cylinder block never moves), the crankshaft with shaft and the connecting rod with rod. Put the three in one group, the crankshaft turning with spin. On a plain cylinder laid on its side as the crankshaft, the crank draws the pin and runs the rod on it in front of the disc: add no pin of your own. pin is which throw (1 is the first).

valve.description: the id of the valve part already added

id.description: the same as valve; valve is clearer

by.description: the id of the camshaft part already added

lift.description: how far it moves down in units (default a fifth of its length); 0.01 to 50

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

cam.description: A valve (or any follower) that a spinning camshaft pushes down along y: it is down by lift while the cam nose points down at it, and back up otherwise. open is how many degrees of the turn of the cam it stays open (default 110), phase the cam angle where it is most open (default 180: the nose pointing down). This acts on parts you have already added, by their ids; it adds nothing and a new name does nothing. Name the valve with valve and the camshaft with by.

by.description: the part whose turning times it

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

flash.description: A glow that comes on at one point of the cycle of a turning part: the object (a small sphere for a spark, a larger one for the burn) is invisible, flares to its opacity at the crank angle given and dies away over span degrees. by is the crankshaft; angle is degrees into a cycle of cycle degrees (default 720, a four-stroke engine: 0 is the piston at the top starting the intake, 360 the top of the compression).

kind.description: left out, the kind of the joint the object has

amount.description: slide: total travel in units; swing: degrees each side; pulse: the size factor (1.3 is 30% bigger, 0.8 smaller); 0.01 to 360

by.description: a spinning part to stay in step with

ratio.description: with by: cycles per turn of that part (default 1); -20 to 20

phase.description: degrees ahead (180 is half a cycle behind another loop at 0); -3600 to 3600

pivot.description: swing: from the object to the point it turns about; [x,y,z], each -100 to 100

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

loop.description: Repeat a motion on any object: slide (back and forth along axis, amount units in all), swing (rock about axis by amount degrees each side, round pivot) or pulse (swell to amount times its size), every period seconds (default 2) or by a spinning part. Left out, kind is the joint's. Another loop replaces it; stop ends it.

pivot.description: hinge: from the object to the point it turns about; [x,y,z], each -100 to 100

to.description: fixed: the object it rides with

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

joint.description: Give any object a freedom: hinge (turns about axis through pivot, the point from the object), slide (along axis or a tilted dir), fixed (rides with to). min and max hold its value. It moves when spin, loop or couple drives it.

pitch.description: units of travel for one turn, between a hinge and a slide; -100 to 100

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

couple.description: One joint follows another: its value is ratio times that of by, plus phase. Use ratio between two of a kind (gear, belt, lever) and pitch between a hinge and a slide (units of travel for one turn: a screw, a rack, a rope on a wheel is 2 x pi x radius). stop ends it.

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

cut.description: Cut a 3D object (usually a whole model) open with a plane, so the inside shows: everything beyond the plane is removed and the cut faces are capped. axis is x, y or z (default z, the plane faces the viewer at the front); to is where the plane is along that axis in the object own space (the middle of the object is 0). Move the plane through with another cut; to 100 puts it beyond everything: no cut.

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

orbit.description: Move the camera around what it looks at: az is the angle around (0 faces the front), el the height angle.

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

zoom.description: Camera distance factor: 1 is the default framing, 2 is twice as close.

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

focus.description: Aim the camera at a 3D object; without id, back at the middle of the stage.

wait.description: Guide mode: once this step has been drawn and spoken, wait for the person to click, and go on to the next step only when the screen has really changed. x,y,w,h is the box (top-left corner and size, on the screenshot) the click should land in; leave it out when it could be anywhere. Draw the target with a mark as well, and give each guide step its own ids.

go.description: Guide mode, optional: let the app make one navigation move for the person, in a step that points at it (the wait stays: if the app does not do it, they click). kind is tab (a tab), open (a menu item that opens a submenu) or scroll (a window or area; dir down by default). x,y is the middle of that control on the screenshot (anywhere in the area for scroll). The app does it only in a native window, only if the person has allowed it, says so aloud first, and refuses everything that is not exactly this (a button, a link, a checkbox, a field, anything that saves, sends, deletes or buys). At most one a step.

at.description: seconds after the step starts; 0 to 60

clear.description: Remove an object or mark (and what is attached to it), or everything with "all", every mark, card, diagram and pin with "marks", the 3D stage and its objects with "panel".

step.description: What is said and what appears while it is said. At most 24 actions.

say.description: The words spoken for this step, up to 400 characters
